title: Surge Harmonizer Control Panel — compact stability + burst controls for dedicated GPU pools
creator: Asha Raman
description: Design a compact, operator-focused control panel for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces pool health, predictive surge controls, and a gated ‘surge harmonizer’ for temporary capacity bursts. The scope includes wireframes, high-fidelity prototype, developer handoff specs, and a short usability test. Goal: enable platform and SRE teams to understand trade-offs (latency vs cost) and safely tune burst/autoscale knobs without leaving the pool detail surface.
decisions: Compact control will live as a right-rail micro-panel on pool details instead of a full-page modal to preserve operator flow (decided 2025-01-30).
Default surge mode set to 'adaptive' with an advanced 'manual surge dial' for power users — reduces accidental cost spikes (agreed 2025-02-03).
Introduce a preview timeline showing predicted latency and cost curves for a chosen burst window (approved by PM 2025-02-07).
Use color-coded thermal band visualization for recent GPU temperature and contention to signal risk for bursts (UX + Eng alignment 2025-02-11).
comments: 2025-01-28 Asha Raman: Initial brief and research notes uploaded. Primary persona: Platform engineer who needs rapid triage and temporary capacity adjustments.
2025-01-30 Miles Ortega: Proposed right-rail placement and three control modes (off, adaptive, manual) — added low-fidelity sketches.
2025-02-02 Priya Kapoor (PM): Asked to include quick 'rollback to baseline' CTA and tie to cost estimates per-minute for bursts.
2025-02-05 Liam Chen (Eng): Raised constraints around live kernel switching during bursts; suggested gating manual bursts behind a safety check to avoid GPU churn.
2025-02-07 Design critique (cross-functional): Need clearer affordance for hysteresis and cooldown; suggested microcopy and inline tooltips.
2025-02-10 Usability test (n=6 ops engineers): Positive for single-panel flow; participants wanted an explicit 'what if' scenario runner. Added to scope.
2025-02-12 Miles Ortega: Updated hi-fi with thermal band, surge dial micro-interactions, and the scenario playback widget. Shared for engineering review.
2025-02-14 Eng review (Liam Chen): API fields required: burst_duration, target_qps, cost_estimate_per_min, safety_token. Asked for clear acceptance criteria for fallback behavior.
2025-02-14 PM review (Priya Kapoor): Requested that the control panel surface SLA impact warning when predicted latency crosses configured SLOs.

accessibility_notes: Ensure surge dial can be operated via keyboard and has ARIA labels for current value and step increments.
Thermal band colors must pass WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio; also provide patterned fill option for color-blind users.
Tooltip content should be readable by screen readers and dismissible via ESC.
Provide text-only summary for rapid incident triage (collapsed state)
visual_specs: Surge dial: 0-100% with 5% step increments and snap points at 25/50/75
Thermal band: three tiers (nominal/warning/critical) with numeric thresholds exposed
Scenario playback: condensed sparkline + latency/cost overlay; frame rate 250ms per step for playback simulation
acceptance_criteria: Clickable prototype demonstrates right-rail panel with three control modes and scenario playback
Engineering tickets created with API fields and example payloads, and agreed fallback behavior
Usability test (n>=5) shows at least 80% of participants can complete a 'create temporary burst' flow without assistance
Accessibility checklist items implemented or documented as exceptions
Telemetry events instrumented for control interactions and visible in staging telemetry dashboard
